summary: Same family — a diagonal-symmetric rainbow XOR/Sierpinski fractal with matching colour and brightness statistics — but the port runs its timers 1.67x (morph cycle) to 3.33x (super-cycle) too fast and draws a measurably different geometry: no time rescale aligns the two, and the port's field snaps exactly to the integer pixel-index XOR while the original's does not.
observations: Both sides compile and render cleanly on the default rig (grid 16x16), no compile or runtime errors, no controls exposed on either side (control surfaces match: both empty).

Both sides are fully deterministic: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce byte-identical dumps per side, and --wall-clock 1756000000 vs 1700000000 is byte-identical too. A faithful port should therefore track the original frame-for-frame; it does not.

Both sides are time-based, not frame-coupled: the same motion-autocorrelation periods come out at 10, 20 and 40 fps (orig 65f/131f/261f = 6.50/6.55/6.53 s; port 39f/79f/157f = 3.90/3.95/3.92 s). No frame-rate coupling on either side.
PRIMARY CYCLE: original's morph cycle is 6.55 s (matches a Pixelblaze time(0.1) = 6.5536 s sawtooth); the port's is 3.93 s (matches time(0.06) = 3.932 s). Port is 1.67x too fast.

SUPER-CYCLE: from the 240 s / 5 fps survey, the original's mean-brightness autocorrelation peaks hard at 65.6 s (corr 0.64) = 10 x 6.55 s, i.e. a full repeat every 65.5 s (time(1.0) = 65.536 s). The port's peaks at 19.6 s (0.74), 39.4 s, 59.0 s, 78.6 s — a full repeat every 19.66 s (time(0.3)). Port is 3.33x too fast on the slow timer. Because 1.67 != 3.33, NO single global speed factor can align the two.

MOTION RATE: port's frame-to-frame motion is consistently ~2x the original's at every rate — 6.2 vs 12.4 (20 fps, 6 s), 13 vs 23 (10 fps), 4 vs 7 (40 fps), 7 vs 13 on the 30 s window. The port visibly flickers/twitches about twice as hard.

TIME-RESCALE FIT FAILS: scanning corr(orig[t], port[k*t]) over k=0.3..2.5 with a phase offset on whole-frame brightness peaks at k~0.59-0.60 with a correlation of only 0.18. Per-frame nearest-neighbour search over each side's FULL super-cycle (269 frames sampled 0.25 s apart across 67 s) gives a median best-match correlation of 0.56 (orig->port) / 0.59 (port->orig), against a control of 0.96 for original frames matched to the original's own repeats >=2 s away. The port's shape vocabulary genuinely differs; this is not phase.

STRUCTURE — GRID QUANTIZATION: on power-of-two grids the PORT's brightness field is EXACTLY a function of (pixelX XOR pixelY): testing v(x,y) == v(0, x^y) gives residual 0.00 at all 27 sampled times on 16x16 and at all 3 sampled times on 8x8. The ORIGINAL never is (residual 15.7-55.9 at the same times). Fitting a quantized XOR scale S on a 48x48 grid, the port fits S=16/32/64 with residual 0.9-1.5 at t=4 s while the original's best residual is 26-40 at any S. Concretely, the original's t=4 s frame has diagonal blocks of unequal sizes 5,3,3,5 across a 16-px row with smooth gradients inside them (row 0: 245 182 185 254 141 55 14 1 0 0 0 1 4 7 7 4); the port's is a clean 2x2 power-of-two lattice (row 0: 15 4 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 3 7 14 26 42 64). The original XORs continuously-scaled coordinates and breathes/zooms; the port's XOR snaps to the pixel grid, giving a more 'digital', aliased look at low resolution.

STRUCTURE — SHARED: both sides are exactly symmetric about the main diagonal (mean |v(x,y)-v(y,x)| = 0.00 at every sampled time on both), and both draw the same vocabulary of nested squares, diamonds, X-diagonals and ring/annulus outlines.
RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE: both sides redraw the same logical picture with finer detail at 48x48 as at 16x16 — neither is native-resolution rasterizing. No divergence on this axis.

COLOUR: essentially identical character. Mean saturation of lit pixels 1.000 on both; hue histograms cover all 12 sectors on both (orig 6.6-11.2% per sector, port 6.0-10.8%); dark-pixel fraction 0.494 (orig) vs 0.441 (port); mean value 44.8 vs 48.2.

BRIGHTNESS ENVELOPE: near-identical distributions over 1360 frames of the 68 s dump run — mean 23.4 vs 24.7, max 108 vs 107, frames with mean <=1: 40 vs 39, <=8: 128 vs 114, >=60: 40 vs 40. Both sides blank to near-black for brief moments a few percent of the time; neither dies, saturates or drifts.

STEADY STATE: healthy on both sides at every window checked — --skip 16, 33, 49 and a 20 s window at --skip 200 all give orig mean 22-27 / motion 7 and port mean 23-26 / motion 13-14. brightnessTrend is volatile/steady on both, no decay.

RIG SWEEP — CLOUD (10x10x10, 1000 px): both sides produce the same kind of dense rainbow filigree of nested arches with dark bands; the port's arches are finer and its evolution faster, but the character matches.

RIG SWEEP — STRIP (non-default): a large divergence in the y-degenerate case. On a 240 px strip the original has 28-46 local brightness maxima and 12.6-23.1 full hue turns across the strip at t = 1/3/5/7 s; the port has exactly 1 maximum and 0.47-1.51 hue turns at the same times — a ~30x spatial-frequency collapse. The 60 px strip waterfall shows it plainly: the original is a dense weave of nested arcs, the port is one or two broad slow sweeping curves. This does NOT reproduce on grid or cloud rigs, so it is specific to the 1D/flat-y degenerate case (and the harness pins z=0.5 there).
feedback: Slow the port down, and note it needs TWO different corrections, not one global factor. The fast/morph timer should have a 6.55 s period (Pixelblaze time(0.1) = 6.5536 s); the port's is 3.93 s (time(0.06)) — 1.67x too fast. The slow/super-cycle timer should have a 65.5 s period (time(1.0) = 65.536 s); the port's is 19.66 s (time(0.3)) — 3.33x too fast. Fixing only one of them will not align the sides.
After the timing fix, expect frame-to-frame motion to drop from ~12 to ~6 at 20 fps on the 16x16 grid; that is the cheapest regression check.

The port quantizes its XOR to the pixel grid: on 8x8 and 16x16 grids its brightness field is exactly v(x,y) = f(pixelX XOR pixelY) at every sampled time (residual 0.00), which locks every block boundary to a power of two. The original never has that property (residual 16-56 at the same times) — its XOR operands are continuously scaled, so block sizes come out unequal (5,3,3,5 across one 16-px row at t=4 s) and drift/breathe over the cycle, with smooth gradients inside each block. Scale the coordinates by a time-varying continuous factor before the XOR rather than by the pixel count.

On a 240 px strip (y degenerate, z pinned 0.5) the original still shows 28-46 brightness maxima and 13-23 hue turns across the strip while the port shows exactly 1 of each. Whatever supplies the original's high spatial frequency when y=0 is missing from the port; check the term that survives when only x varies.

Nothing needs changing in colour or brightness: full saturation, full rainbow hue coverage, dark fraction, mean and peak brightness, and the frequency of near-black moments all already match the original within a few percent. The diagonal (x<->y) symmetry and the resolution-independent drawing are also already correct.

The pattern is fully deterministic — seed- and wall-clock-independent on both sides, and fps-invariant on both — so once the timers and the XOR scaling are right, the port should be checkable against the original with near-byte-identical dumps rather than statistics.
